newsitem.title: USA: Duke McGuire 2 nuke seen at full power Wed.
newsitem.headline: Duke McGuire 2 nuke seen at full power Wed.

text.p: Duke Power Co's 1,129 megawatt (MW) McGuire nuclear power unit 2 was likely to reach full output today, returning from an outage which began Oct 31, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
The Cornelius, N.C., unit was operating at 98 percent of capacity as of Wednesday morning and was likely to reach full power later in the day, spokesman Rick Zuercher said.
The adjoining 1,129 MW McGuire nuclear power unit 1 returned to full power earlier this week.
Both units were shut down Oct 31 after one of the facility's four backup battery banks failed to meet performance criteria during a test.
Separately, Duke's Oconee nuclear power facility in Seneca, S.C., remained shut following a steam pipe rupture in September.
The 846 MW Oconee unit 1 and the 846 MW Oconee unit 2 were roughly expected to return to serivce near the end of December, Zuercher said.
The 846 MW Oconee unit 3 was likely to return to service in January, the spokesman said.
Oconee 3 is undergoing scheduled refueling and maintenance but was shut early for scrutiny following the September accident.
